content.title: About
content.content: Turkey neck is meat taken from the cervical region of the bird. It has a rich flavor, moderate fat content, and a firm texture. The neck is commonly used for braising, roasting, and making stocks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey neck contains more connective tissue, making it especially tender when cooked slowly.
In many traditional cuisines the neck is considered a delicacy and is often served at festive meals.
The meat is rich in collagen, which is beneficial for skin and joint health.
When properly marinated, the neck can acquire a flavor similar to breast meat but with a deeper, meatier note.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Turkey neck provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamins B3, B6 and B12, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: The neck supplies iron, zinc and phosphorus, which are essential for blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Like most meats, turkey neck contains virtually no carbs, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to poultry meat.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: The neck is fattier than the breast, so those monitoring fat intake should watch portion sizes.

items.title: Thorough cooking required
items.content: As with any meat, turkey neck must be cooked to a safe internal temperature to avoid food‑borne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Turkey neck can be braised in sauce, roasted with herbs, cooked in a slow cooker, or used to make a flavorful broth. Marinating it in olive oil, spices and lemon juice before cooking enhances tenderness and taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh turkey neck refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in an airtight bag at ‑18 °C, where it remains good for up to 6 months. Thaw frozen neck in the refrigerator before cooking.
